title: Evaluating the Representation Space of Diffusion Models via Self-Supervised Principles
claim: One self-supervised diagnostic metric, computed from invariant and residual feature components, unifies representation quality, generation quality, and memorization detection.
layout: 3 panels: (a) metric pipeline, (b) intuition cartoon, (c) three result plots
description: The figure has three rounded, lavender-bordered panels. Panel (a), top left, shows a training photo being augmented and noised into three views. Each view goes through a feature extractor and is split into a green invariant bar (s) and a hatched blue residual (ξ). To the right, covariance definitions, a purple bar chart of Fisher SNR eigenvalues and the ICR formula in a shaded box are stacked vertically. Panel (b), top right, is a two-column cartoon. Low ICR shows tight clusters of blue views around red means that are spread far apart. High ICR shows scattered views around means that bunch together. Panel (c), along the bottom, has three line plots with dual axes. The first plots ICR against classification accuracy over noise level. The second plots ICR against FID over training. The third plots ICR against memorization ratio. Each plot has a shaded title banner. The eye lands first on the photo and arrows, then moves to the plots.
caption: \textbf{Overview of the $\mathrm{ICR}$ Framework}. Each training image is augmented and passed through the diffusion feature extractor, decomposing representations into an invariant component $\bm s$ and a residual $\bm \xi$; their covariances define $\mathrm{ICR}$ (a–b). $\mathrm{ICR}$ serves as a unified diagnostic: it identifies the optimal noise level for classification tasks, tracks generative quality without sampling, and anticipates memorization onset during training (c).
abstract: Diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generative capabilities and have also emerged as powerful self-supervised representation learners, yet the connection between these two abilities remains less explored. Drawing inspiration from self-supervised learning (SSL), we introduce a framework for jointly evaluating the representation and generation capabilities of diffusion models. Specifically, we decompose features into invariant and residual components and derive the Invariant Contamination Ratio (ICR), a Fisher-based metric that quantifies how residual variation contaminates invariant signal in feature space. We use this framework to analyze both discriminative and generative behavior of diffusion models. On the representation side, we find that invariance peaks at intermediate noise levels, which also yield the best downstream classification performance. On the generative side, we study how training transitions from genuine generalization to memorization in data-limited regimes, and show that ICR serves as a sensitive training-time indicator of early learning: increasing residual energy along Fisher directions marks the onset of memorization, detectable from training features alone without external evaluators or held-out test sets. Overall, our results show that diffusion models can be monitored from a self-supervised perspective through the geometry of their learned representations.
